speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what progress the Ministry has made since February 2025 in developing and implementing sector-specific advertising guidelines for tuition and private education services; (b) whether a code of conduct has been finalised; (c) what its key provisions are; and (d) how the Ministry will monitor and enforce compliance to protect parents and students from fear-based marketing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The code requires advertisements to be legal, decent, honest and truthful, and be prepared with a sense of responsibility to the consumer and society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Tuition and other private education providers should comply with this code in their advertisements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We understand that some of these anxieties stem from the perceived stakes of academic grades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
text: To address this and to better support the holistic development of our students, MOE has made shifts in the education landscape to reduce the over-emphasis on academic results.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: One, I understand there is a general code of conduct for advertisements.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Similar to the medical practice where there is a specific set of guidelines for medical practices, is the Ministry looking at a specific set of guidelines for private education and tuition centres?

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: Will the Ministry be doing anything to address this as well?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I do note that as far as tuition is concerned, it can drive a fair bit of anxiety in our parents as well as our students, and I can understand where he is coming from.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The other aspect in relation to education is also this: we are working towards the holistic development of our students and we recognise that an over-emphasis on academic results alone will not do justice to that.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: So, the focus of MOE has always been towards a holistic education, wherein we also want to build the social-emotional competencies of our students to develop alongside the 21st Century Competencies, which include critical as well as innovative thinking, and at the same time, the ability to communicate and collaborate as students in schools.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Our desire is when we look at education, it is not merely just about academic grades alone, but also about the holistic development of the child.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: This is something we continue to encourage in our children as well as message to our parents.
